projects.title: Crypto Trading Bot
projects.subtitle: Automated cryptocurrency trading bot for Binance.us
projects.shortDescription: A Python trading bot that runs SMA-crossover and RSI strategies against Binance.us, with regime-aware strategy switching, layered risk controls, CSV-based trade tracking, and a local Flask dashboard. It has run live and logged real trades.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Built an automated cryptocurrency trading bot that connects to Binance.us and trades a fixed set of USDT pairs (BTC, ETH, ADA, SOL, DOGE, SHIB) on a recurring loop. Each cycle it pulls recent candles, computes indicators, classifies the market regime, evaluates a buy/sell/hold signal, applies risk gates, and places limit orders when conditions allow.

The bot is a single-account system written in Python. It stores all state in CSV files rather than a database—reconstructing open positions from the trade log on each cycle—so it can be stopped and restarted safely. It has run live against a real Binance.us account and logged actual trades and daily portfolio snapshots.

sections.title: Key Features
list: SMA-crossover entry/exit signals confirmed by RSI, implemented as modular strategy classes.
Regime-aware behavior: a defensive strategy blocks new buys during detected crashes or high-volatility conditions.
Time-of-day strategy switching—an aggressive profile on 1-minute candles during set UTC hours, a moderate profile on 15-minute candles otherwise.
Layered risk controls: a minimum portfolio floor, market-crash detection, a BTC 'canary' check, and ATR-based stop-loss / take-profit levels.
CSV-based persistence for trade history and daily balance snapshots; positions are inferred from the log rather than held in memory.
Local Flask dashboard (vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with Chart.js) showing portfolio value, realized/unrealized P&L, win rate, per-asset balances, and an activity log.
Optional Discord webhook notifications for trade fills, risk blocks, daily summaries, and errors.

sections.title: My Contributions
list: Designed the recurring trading loop and the separation between the API client, indicators, strategies, risk engine, and logging.
Implemented the Binance.us integration using python-binance (candles, balances, exchange rules, and limit orders).
Wrote the SMA/RSI strategy, the defensive strategy, and the regime-based strategy selector.
Built the risk engine: portfolio floor, crash detection, BTC canary, and ATR-derived stop-loss/take-profit.
Implemented CSV trade and balance logging plus the position-reconstruction logic that survives restarts.
Built the local Flask dashboard and the optional Discord notification layer.
Iteratively tuned strategy parameters—candle granularity, SMA lengths, and RSI thresholds—based on live behavior.

sections.title: Technologies Used
paragraphs: Python, python-binance (Binance.us API), Flask, pandas, Chart.js, Discord webhooks, CSV-based storage

sections.title: Honest Scope
paragraphs: This is a working single-user bot, not a multi-tenant platform. It trades one Binance.us account, stores data in CSV files (no database), and has no backtesting engine or multi-exchange support. The dashboard runs locally and API keys are read from a local .env file.

projects.title: Stock Trading Bots
projects.subtitle: Two rule-based stock trading bots built on the Alpaca API
projects.shortDescription: Two iterations of an automated stock trading bot built on Alpaca paper trading. The first is a Flask-based momentum/trend trader; the second is a FastAPI service that scans 300+ symbols with technical indicators and uses a local LLM to explain its trades. Both are rule-based and run in paper or simulated mode.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Built two versions of an automated stock trading bot on top of the Alpaca brokerage API, both defaulting to paper trading. The goal was to analyze live market data, generate rule-based signals, and execute trades under explicit risk controls—logging everything for review. Neither version uses machine learning to make trading decisions; the strategies are deterministic, indicator-based rules.

The two versions share the same philosophy but differ in architecture: the first is a Flask-based momentum and trend trader; the second is a FastAPI service that scans a much larger universe, validates trades through a dedicated risk engine, and adds a local LLM that writes plain-language explanations of each trade.

sections.title: Version 1 — Flask Momentum/Trend Bot
list: Long-only strategy: enters when price is above its 20-day moving average with positive short-term momentum, above-average volume, and a bullish SPY market filter.
Exits on a stop loss, take profit, loss of trend, or fading momentum.
Risk controls: a maximum number of concurrent positions, a per-position size cap, dynamic position sizing, and a daily loss limit.
CSV logging of trades, signals, equity, positions, errors, and daily summaries, with retention-based cleanup and gzip backups.
A watchdog thread auto-restarts the bot if the main loop stalls, alongside a Flask dashboard (later deactivated in favor of Alpaca's own) and optional Discord notifications.

sections.title: Version 2 — FastAPI Scanner Bot with Local LLM
list: FastAPI + APScheduler service that scans 300+ S&P 500 / NASDAQ-100 symbols on a recurring cycle during market hours.
Computes ~13 technical indicators (SMA, EMA, RSI, MACD, ATR, VWAP, momentum, relative volume) and ranks opportunities before generating signals via a multi-factor voting system.
A risk engine validates each candidate trade on spread, liquidity, and a risk-reward ratio that adapts to volatility, then places bracket (OCO) orders with attached stop-loss and take-profit.
Runs in LEARNING (simulated), PAPER (real Alpaca paper orders), or LIVE mode—LIVE is intentionally gated off in code behind hard safety checks.
A local Ollama model (qwen2.5-coder:7b) generates concise, human-readable explanations of placed trades for the logs and dashboard—explanation only, never used to decide trades.
CSV logging of trades, signals, rankings, AI explanations, and daily summaries, with Discord weekly summaries and error alerts.

sections.title: My Contributions
list: Designed both bots' architectures—separating market-data access, strategy logic, risk validation, order execution, and logging.
Implemented the Alpaca integrations (account, bars, positions, market and bracket orders) for paper trading.
Wrote the rule-based strategies: the momentum/trend logic in v1 and the indicator-voting signal generation in v2.
Built the risk controls in both versions, including v2's adaptive risk-reward engine and bracket-order stops/targets.
Integrated a local Ollama LLM in v2 to produce plain-language trade explanations without affecting trading decisions.
Implemented CSV-based logging, retention/cleanup, watchdog auto-restart, and Discord notifications.
Built Flask and FastAPI dashboards for monitoring (both later deprioritized in favor of Alpaca's native dashboard).

sections.title: Technologies Used
paragraphs: Python, Alpaca API (alpaca-py), FastAPI, Flask, APScheduler, pandas, numpy, the 'ta' indicator library, Ollama (local qwen2.5-coder LLM), Chart.js, CSV-based storage, Discord webhooks

sections.title: Honest Scope
paragraphs: Both bots run in paper or simulated mode; live trading is either untested or deliberately disabled in code. Neither includes a backtesting engine, and data is stored in CSV files rather than a database. The signals are rule-based—the LLM only narrates trades, it does not make them.

projects.title: Portfolio & Resume Website
projects.subtitle: Data-driven static portfolio and résumé site
projects.shortDescription: A content-driven portfolio built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. All copy and structure are defined in JSON; a single script detects the URL, loads the right data, and renders the page—no build step.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Designed and built a clean, minimal portfolio website to present my resume, professional experience, and technical projects. The site is fully data-driven: content lives in JSON files under data/, and a shared content script (content.js) determines the page type from the URL, fetches the appropriate JSON, and injects the rendered HTML into a single root element. Adding or editing projects, experience, skills, or service entries requires only JSON and an HTML shell file per detail page—no build or CMS.

sections.title: Site Structure
paragraphs: Static HTML shells (index, experience/index, projects/index, skills, education, service/index, contact) each contain a nav, a main content root, and a footer. The script infers page type (home, list, or detail) from the path and filename. Home shows a hero (name, intro, profile image), a tech stack logo grid from techstack.json, and a Featured Experience section (one experience plus up to two projects, configured in site.json). List pages render cards from the corresponding JSON; detail pages (e.g. projects/slug.html, experience/slug.html, service/slug.html) resolve the slug from the URL, find the matching entry in JSON, and render the full detail view. All links, resume path, and featured IDs are controlled via site.json and the data README documents which file controls what.

sections.title: Key Features
list: Fully data-driven: site.json, projects.json, experience.json, skills.json, techstack.json, education.json, service.json, and contact.json control all content; no content in HTML.
Single content renderer (content.js) handles home, list, and detail pages via URL-based routing and fetch of JSON.
Detail pages use one static HTML file per slug (e.g. projects/ella-rises.html); the script loads projects.json and renders the project with that slug—no build step.
Home includes a configurable tech stack grid and clickable Featured Experience cards that link to the corresponding experience or project detail pages.
Deployed as a static site on GitHub Pages with a GitHub Actions workflow and optional custom domain (CNAME).
Modular CSS (main.css, responsive.css), shared nav and footer injected from site data, and responsive layout with reveal animations.

sections.title: Technologies Used
paragraphs: HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, JSON, GitHub Pages, GitHub Actions
